chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Bint Ilyās, who said:
I heard him saying: I saw my father, عليه السلام, when he had a nosebleed after he had performed wudu (ablution), with flowing blood, so he performed wudu (ablution).

So it may bear several possibilities: one of them is that it be interpreted as a case of taqiyyah, according to what we have previously stated regarding it; the second is that we interpret it as recommendation rather than obligation; and the third is that we interpret it as washing the affected place, because that is also called wudu (ablution), as we have explained in Kitāb Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām. And what indicates this meaning is that which...

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection in circumstances requiring caution

ai.seo_question: Does a nosebleed invalidate wudu (ablution) according to this hadith from al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This report concerns the ruling on nosebleed after wudu (ablution), mentioning that the Imam عليه السلام performed wudu (ablution) again after flowing blood emerged. The accompanying discussion explains that the report may be understood in multiple ways: as taqiyyah, as indicating recommendation rather than obligation, or as referring only to washing the affected area.
